A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
soil aggregate size and the presence of organic debris have a strong impact on the function of the methanogens but a small impact on their community structure.
the methanogenic activity of rice field soil is limited by the availability of substrates and not by the structure of the microbial community.
the structure of the community is not a good predictor for the function of the community.
The main takeaway from our work is that

soil aggregate size has an important impact on the function and the structure of the microbial community, but that the effect of the different aggregate sizes is not due to a different distribution of the archaeal community among the aggregates.

soil aggregate size has a strong effect on methane production, which is likely to be caused by differences in organic carbon content, substrate availability and the distribution of methanogenic microorganisms.
the structure of methanogenic communities is not necessarily affected by the size and composition of soil aggregates.
